chapter: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
title: Mike Jackson, Victor sessions in 1927 and Fats Waller on organ
summary: Pianist-songwriter Mike Jackson sold his songs cheaply; she recorded with him for Victor, and with Fats Waller on pipe organ in Camden in May 1927.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now, who was Mike Jackson, with whom you (Inaudible)?

Mike Jackson was a piano player, and he wrote a lot of songs. He was in Chicago, Mike Jackson. He wrote a lot of good songs, and I didn't know -- and he never did get any credit for them. I think he sold most all of them for a few dollars.

Well, you recorded with him for Victor -- 'I'll Forgive You Because I Love You,' 'I'm Going to Lose Myself Way Down in Louisville,' 'My Old Daddy's Got a Brand New Way to Love,' and 'I'm Down Right Now, But I Won't be Down Always.'
And some of those were mine, you know.
They were? And that was in February of '27. Then in May of '27 you did three sides with Fats Waller on the pipe organ, which you did in Camden. Do you remember that?
Uh-huh, I made that with Fats -- it was 'Memphis Blues' --
-- and 'I'm Going To See My Ma'.
'Going To See My Ma', yeah, I made them
with Fats Waller playing the organ.
Oh, you have? I have two of them. I have "Sugar" and "Beale Street Blues."
Yeah -- no, I just got the little things they first made.
